cornea.name: Cornea
cornea.description: Transparent anterior dome of the sclera that allows light to enter and provides the major refraction (bending) of incoming light rays.

pupil.name: Pupil
pupil.description: Central circular opening in the iris through which light passes into the posterior chamber of the eye.

iris.name: Iris
iris.description: Pigmented muscular ring containing antagonistic circular and radial muscles that regulate pupil aperture (pupillary reflex).

biconvex_lens.name: Biconvex Lens
biconvex_lens.description: Transparent, flexible biconvex disc that alters its curvature to fine-focus light rays onto the photoreceptors of the retina (accommodation).

ciliary_body.name: Ciliary Body & Muscle
ciliary_body.description: Thickened ring of vascular tissue and smooth muscle that contracts and relaxes to control tension on the suspensory ligaments during accommodation.

suspensory_ligaments.name: Suspensory Ligaments (Zonules)
suspensory_ligaments.description: Inelastic fibrous strands connecting the ciliary body to the lens capsule, transmitting mechanical tension to flatten or round the lens.

retina.name: Retina (Photoreceptive Layer)
retina.description: Innermost sensory tunic containing light-sensitive photoreceptor cells (rods for dim monochrome vision and cones for acute colour vision).

choroid.name: Choroid
choroid.description: Darkly pigmented, highly vascular middle tunic that absorbs internal reflections of light and supplies oxygen and nutrients to retinal cells.

sclera.name: Sclera
sclera.description: Tough, opaque, fibrous outer white layer that protects delicate inner structures and maintains the spherical intraocular shape of the eyeball.

fovea_centralis.name: Fovea Centralis (Yellow Spot)
fovea_centralis.description: Depressed central area of the retina with the densest packing of cones and zero rods, producing maximum visual acuity.

blind_spot.name: Blind Spot (Optic Disc)
blind_spot.description: Region of the retina where nerve fibers converge to form the optic nerve; devoid of photoreceptors, creating an insensitive area in visual field.

optic_nerve.name: Optic Nerve (Cranial Nerve II)
optic_nerve.description: Thick sensory nerve bundle carrying action potentials generated by photoreceptors to the visual cortex of the occipital lobe in the brain.
